div.p: In the course of the discussions leading to the Agreement signed this day, the United States Government have asked for a reduction in the preference accorded in the United Kingdom to Empire tobacco. The Government of the United Kingdom have recognised that this request is one to which the United States Government have attached much importance but they have been prevented from entertaining it by the existence of Agreements with several Governments within the British Empire which guarantee continuance of the present margin of preference until August, 1942.

The two Governments note that the increase in the importation into the United Kingdom of Empire tobacco in recent years has not led to a diminution in the importation of United States tobacco and the Government of the United Kingdom undertake that, if there is a material change in this position during the currency of this Agreement, they will be prepared before decisions are taken as to the level of the preference after August, 1942, to examine afresh the possibility of making some reduction in the margin of preference.
